sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and the 'Pulmonary Mask' Phenomenon
sections.description: This section introduces the case by detailing the initial respiratory symptoms (dyspnea, chest pain, recurrent right-sided effusions) that mimicked primary thoracic pathology. It explores the concept of the 'pulmonary mask,' where pancreatic disease presents exclusively with respiratory signs, often leading to misdiagnosis. The narrative follows the three admissions, highlighting how the initial focus on tuberculosis and pneumonia diverted attention from the true abdominal etiology.
subtopics: Initial presentation: Recurrent right-sided pleural effusion and respiratory distress
The 'Pulmonary Mask': Why pancreatic pathology masquerades as lung disease
Red herrings: TB contact history and elevated ADA leading to empirical anti-TB therapy
The critical clue: Uncovering the history of blunt abdominal trauma (bicycle handle)
Characteristics of the fluid: Dark red, blood-stained pleural effusion

sections.description: This section provides a focused explanation of how a Pancreatopleural Fistula (PPF) develops, specifically in the context of pediatric trauma versus genetic etiologies. It details the anatomical pathways allowing pancreatic enzymes to traverse from the retroperitoneum to the pleural space, emphasizing why this specific mechanism results in massive, enzyme-rich effusions rather than simple ascites.
subtopics: Anatomical route: Retroperitoneal tracking through esophageal/aortic hiatuses
Mechanism of rupture: Ductal disruption vs. pseudocyst erosion following trauma
Pediatric vs. Adult epidemiology: Trauma and genetics (PRSS1/SPINK1) vs. Alcoholism
Biochemical cascade: How pancreatic enzymes cause tissue damage and hemorrhage in the pleura

sections.description: This section walks through the stepwise diagnostic process required to distinguish PPF from other causes of high-amylase pleural effusions. It contrasts non-specific findings (CT showing consolidation/hydropneumothorax) with definitive evidence provided by biochemical analysis and advanced imaging (MRCP). The logic moves from ruling out common differentials (TB, malignancy, Boerhaave's) to confirming the pancreatic origin.
subtopics: Key diagnostic pivot point: Pleural fluid amylase >1000 IU/L as a pathognomonic sign
Differentiating amylase types: Pancreatic vs. Salivary sources in differential diagnosis
Role of Cross-sectional Imaging: CT limitations vs. MRCP visualization of fistula tracts
Excluding mimics: Tuberculosis, malignancy, esophageal perforation, and hepatic hydrothorax

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Management Algorithm: From Conservative to Surgical
sections.description: Here, we discuss the management hierarchy for PPF in children. Since standardized guidelines are lacking due to rarity, this section outlines the consensus-based approach starting with aggressive medical management (bowel rest, octreotide). It explains the physiological rationale behind these treatments—suppressing exocrine secretion to allow fistula closure—and defines criteria for escalating to endoscopic or surgical interventions.
